title: Adaptive token-floor simulations and enterprise questionnaire mapping
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Run a set of adaptive simulations to evaluate per-direction (ingress vs egress) token floors, streaming minimums, and grace-credit mechanics while simultaneously producing a mapping document that answers typical enterprise security & procurement questionnaire items. Goal: produce defensible pricing levers that can be offered in enterprise contracts and a single source of truth for legal/solutions teams about how experiment variants map to security/Q&A artifacts.
background: We receive frequent enterprise RFPs where customers ask for billing mechanics and guarantees (minimums, burst handling, streaming discounts) alongside security controls (data residency, audit logs, KMS usage). Current pricing experiments focus on economics, but sales/legal keep asking for explicit mappings between pricing variants and questionnaire answers. This ticket ties the simulation outputs to a questionnaire mapping and defines experiment variants intended for enterprise pilots.
hypotheses: H1: Directional token floors that weight egress 1.4x vs ingress reduce host cost variance without materially degrading perceived fairness for upload-heavy customers.
H2: Introducing a short streaming grace window (first 30s free of floor charges) increases signups for streaming-heavy trials by >8% without increasing net revenue loss beyond 2%.
H3: Providing an enterprise-facing deterministic mapping doc (Q&A) will reduce procurement cycle time by at least one week for pilot contracts.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation results for at least 3 directional-floor variants and 2 streaming-grace variants with ROI metrics (change in gross margin, mean latency, error rate).
A completed questionnaire-mapping doc that answers the top 25 questions from our standard enterprise template and cites the experiment variant(s) that satisfy each commitment.
A recommended default pricing rule (one variant) for sales to offer in pilots and an opt-in process for non-default variants.
Security review sign-off documented and included in attachments.
Instrumentation and telemetry to detect inadvertent revenue regressions during pilot rollout with alerting thresholds configured.
experiment_plan: Design three floor variants: Symmetric floor (baseline), Egress-weighted (egress factor 1.4), Input-weighted (ingress factor 1.2).
Design two streaming grace variants: No-grace, 30s grace window for session starts. Include server-side toggles to enable per-account rule.
Create synthetic workload traces from recent 12-week production telemetry (sampling 2,000 active customers) to run through cost model with sequence-length distributions.
Run Monte Carlo simulations (N=10k) per variant to estimate 95% CI for gross margin and customer cost delta.
Select 3 candidate enterprise customers for closed pilot (solutions-led) and map variant eligibility to contract clauses.
telemetry_metrics: Gross margin delta (variant vs baseline) — reported weekly
Median and 95th percentile latency for streaming sessions
Percent of sessions impacted by grace window
Churn / pilot opt-out rate for customers enrolled
Revenue delta and month-over-month ARR impact estimate
rollout_plan: Run offline simulations and produce a quantitative recommendation (Week 1-2).
Legal + Security Q&A draft produced and reviewed (Week 2).
Enable server-side feature flags for variants; run closed pilot with 3 customers for 6 weeks (Week 3-8).
Monitor telemetry and weekly reviews with Sales/Finance/Legal; if revenue loss >3% or latency degradation >10% at p<0.05, rollback variant.
Produce final recommendation and contract language snippets for CSM/Sales (Week 9).
legal_questions: How does a directional floor impact invoicing line items and audit trails? -> Provide mapping: floor type -> invoice reconciliation steps.
Can grace credits be audited and exported for SOC2 evidence? -> Yes; we will provide CSV exports and tie to request IDs.
Does the streaming grace window change data retention or logging behavior? -> No. All logs retained per standard retention; grace is purely billing logic in the control plane.
How do we guarantee per-tenant isolation for Dedicated customers if variant applied in hosted? -> Document fallback and dedicated-only clauses.
KMS/HSM impacts for billed artifacts (receipts) and where encryption keys are used -> Map design to KMS integration options.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers perceive directional floors as discriminatory -> Mitigation: provide transparent examples and an online estimator + opt-in by default for enterprise pilots.
Risk: Complex billing increases ticket volume -> Mitigation: provide automated reconciliation reports and one-click dispute templates for Billing team.
Risk: Security reviewers flag control-plane telemetry exposure -> Mitigation: include encrypted export endpoints and minimal-identifiers mode for reports.
stakeholders: Eng leads: Miguel Torres (serving-runtime), Jun Park (billing infra)
